# Slowest Key.

@example The hold times are 4, 2, 7 and 2; the third keystroke, on o, is held longest.
[4,6,13,15]
"glow"
=> "o"

@example The keystrokes on b and r are both held for 5, and r comes later in the alphabet.
[5,8,13,16]
"bury"
=> "r"

@example The four strikes of t add up to 8, but each is held for only 2; the keystroke on m is held for 7.
[2,4,6,8,15]
"ttttm"
=> "m"

# The fewest presses, equally long.
[1,2]
"ab"
=> "b"

# The first press, timed from 0, is the only longest; z is short.
[10,11,13]
"kza"
=> "k"

# The first press ties with a later one, whose letter is smaller...
[6,9,15]
"qxa"
=> "q"

# ... or larger.
[6,9,15]
"dxp"
=> "p"

# Three presses tie; the latest letter is the middle one.
[7,14,15,22]
"gsbm"
=> "s"

# h is pressed three times, for 5, 5 and 1: it ties with itself.
[5,6,11,12,14]
"hzhhb"
=> "h"

# All presses equally long: the latest letter of the whole string.
[2,4,6,8,10,12]
"python"
=> "y"

# Every press on the same key.
[3,7,20,21]
"kkkk"
=> "k"

# The last press is the longest.
[1,2,3,1000]
"zyxa"
=> "a"

# The largest times: a press of 999999999 at the end, then at the start.
[1,1000000000]
"mb"
=> "b"

[999999999,1000000000]
"ts"
=> "t"

# A press of 65537 against one of 3: a 16-bit time would wrap to 1.
[65537,65540]
"xa"
=> "x"
